correctness.rationale: The proof uses the exact reduced numerator identity Q_{j+1}=(u_{j-1}+v_{j-1})^2/gcd(h,u_j). Every nontrivial gcd destroys integer-square status by an odd or negative prime valuation. For each p^alpha||h, only x0 of exact p-adic valuation alpha can give a post-initial zero, and one residue modulo p^(alpha+1) corresponds to each unit residue. Negative and positive valuation alternatives both escape and never hit. First-zero orbits are of depth at most p-1. CRT and idempotent monomial reduction count the union of local singleton obstruction sets, proving periodicity and rational density. Standard-library exhaustive verifier checked h=1,2,4,5,10,13,17,25,29,65,145 and the h=145 pattern counts; the unbounded statement rests on proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating full text explicitly poses density of exactly j nonsquare terms as Question 1 of Section 7, after proving only a per-prime at-most-one-failure statement and describing finite-field zero preimages. This new full index-set generating law computes those densities for all h and handles cross-prime index collisions (h=145 gives 12 coincident obstructions). Own recoverable earlier claim dbb6afaf-e2e9-495f-8dba-3929ae25a084 concerns only a special prime class with at most one possible bad index, so it is strictly subsumed and does not imply this unrestricted multi-index theorem. published-finding corpus queries matched other rational dynamical or CRT counting phenomena, none known to imply this statement. The companion preprint referenced by the source was not located, recorded as a genuine residual risk.

value.rationale: Resolves a specific distribution question openly stated by the source, determining every exact set of bad indices for all positive h, with finite CRT period and computable rational densities. The novel collision structure is mathematically necessary: the two-prime h=145 example has 32 two-prime obstruction classes but only 20 with two distinct failures. This is not a textbook coprimality restatement, arbitrary parameter slice, or a computation without object motivation.
